about: What jev is asked about each PR. Changing anything here classifies every PR again on the next run. The wording is adapted from brunobat's quarkus-pr-wall (Apache-2.0); see NOTICE. A yes/no question's yesTone says how its bar reads on the wall (good, bad or quiet); it isn't sent to jev. A question with optionsFrom takes its options from the repo's context file. filter puts a choice on the wall as a filter.

questions.label: Kind of change
questions.text: What does this PR's diff mainly do? Judge from the code, not from what a title or description would claim.

options.bugfix: It corrects behaviour that was wrong.
options.feature: It adds a new capability, API or configuration.
options.refactor: It restructures code without meaning to change behaviour.
options.test-only: It only adds or changes tests or test infrastructure.
options.build-ci: It changes build tooling, CI workflows or release scripts, not shipped code.
options.dependency-upgrade: It mainly bumps dependency or BOM versions.

questions.label: Area
questions.text: Which part of the repository does this PR mainly change, judged from the changed file paths and hunks?

questions.label: Size
questions.text: How large is this change in substance, regardless of how many lines it touches?

options.trivial: Trivial or mechanical: a typo, a rename, a version bump, generated or repeated edits.
options.small: Small and local: one idea in one place.
options.large: Large or intricate: a new flow, or many interacting changes to follow.

questions.label: Blast radius
questions.text: If this change is wrong, how far can it affect the code and the users that depend on it?

options.isolated: Isolated: a test, a sample, docs, or code nothing else calls.
options.module: Within one module: callers inside it, nothing outside.
options.component: One component or extension and the applications that use it.
options.cross-cutting: Many components: an SPI, a shared library, or code most components call.
options.foundational: Everything: the core, the build, security, or the dependency versions every user gets.

questions.label: Changes behaviour
questions.text: Does this PR change the runtime behaviour of the software?
questions.yes: it changes code that runs, configuration read at runtime, or dependency versions that are shipped
questions.no: it only changes documentation, comments, formatting, tests, or build/CI tooling that does not affect the shipped artifact

questions.label: Tests reach the change
questions.text: How much of the changed runtime code do the tests this PR adds or modifies execute?

options.all: Every changed runtime code path is executed by a changed test.
options.some: Some changed runtime code paths are executed by a changed test; others are not.
options.none: The PR changes runtime behaviour and adds or modifies tests, but they execute none of the changed runtime code.
options.no-runtime-change: The PR changes no runtime behaviour, whether or not it changes tests.
options.no-test-changes: The PR changes runtime behaviour but adds or modifies no tests.
options.undetermined: The diff does not give enough to tell, e.g. binary or generated changes, behaviour too indirect to trace, or tests that depend on code outside the diff.

questions.label: Tests assert it
questions.text: Do the tests this PR adds or modifies assert the outcome of the changed code they execute?

options.all: Every changed path the changed tests execute has its outcome asserted.
options.some: Some executed changed paths are asserted; others are only called, built or smoke-run.
options.none: The changed tests execute changed code but assert none of its outcomes.
options.no-runtime-change: The PR changes no runtime behaviour, whether or not it changes tests.
options.no-test-changes: The PR changes runtime behaviour but adds or modifies no tests.
options.no-changed-code-reached: The PR changes runtime behaviour and tests, but the changed tests execute none of the changed runtime code.
options.undetermined: The diff does not give enough to tell.

questions.label: Weakens tests
questions.text: Does this PR remove, disable or loosen existing tests or assertions?
questions.yes: it deletes an existing test or assertion, disables or skips a test, loosens an expected value, or swaps a strict assertion for a weaker one
questions.no: it leaves every existing test and assertion at least as strict as it was, or touches no existing test
